subject: Deployment contracts + GitLab stage gating for isolated VLANs
messages:
From: Kyle Turner <kyle@acme-edge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.procure@acme-edge.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy — contract items + CI gating for VLAN segregation

Hi Priyom / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We circulated a draft deployment contract and a proposed GitLab pipeline that gates changes per-environment. Two asks before procurement:

1) We need confirmation that the GitLab stages enforce the VLAN allocation contract — specifically that any Terraform change touching networking requires a mandatory "network-owner" approval and a pipeline job that runs a policy linter.
2) On the on-prem side, our security team requires an explicit artifact mirroring step (air-gapped registry) and an Ansible step that validates secrets are only read from an approved KMS path.

I've attached the draft contract (iac-contract-v3.pdf) and the proposed GitLab CI (gitlab-ci-stages.yaml). Can your infra/security folks validate and call out any blocking items?

Appreciate a quick check — procurement is scheduled for next Friday.

—Kyle
Acme Edge Systems
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
To: Kyle Turner <kyle@acme-edge.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — contract items + CI gating for VLAN segregation

Kyle — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. Looping in Irene and Marcus from Private Deploy / Networking to validate the gating and IaC contracts. Quick notes from my side:

- We can require a "network-owner" codeowner + an approval job in GitLab, but the linter needs to run policy checks against your company-specific module input (CIDR allocation, reserved ranges). I added a couple of comments in gitlab-ci-stages.yaml (see MR link in related_links).
- Air-gap artifact mirroring is doable; we need the registry sync job to run in a secure runner that has no outbound IPs except the mirror target — recommend a dedicated runner group for air-gapped syncs.
- For Ansible/KMS, we will reject playbooks that call ansible-vault with local password files. All secrets should be referenced via a KMS-backed credential helper; we'll add a pipeline validation job to enforce that.

Irene / Marcus: can you validate the Terraform module contract doc (attached) for the VLAN/CIDR guardrails? Also call out any additional CI blockers we should flag to Acme procurement.

Thanks — Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Kyle Turner <kyle@acme-edge.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.procure@acme-edge.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — contract items + CI gating for VLAN segregation

Thanks Priyom. Read the contract and the terraform-module-contracts.md attachment. Summary of my review:

- Module contracts: good separation of responsibilities. We ask that each network module declare:
  * "cidr_block_owner" (team email)
  * "reserved_prefixes" (list)
  * "allowlist_subnets" boolean (must be explicit)

- Policy enforcement: we'll add a pipeline job that invokes a pre-commit/policy linter (custom OPA check) that validates the module inputs against a company-level prefix registry. That job must run before plan is allowed to proceed.

- Workspaces: require separate Terraform workspaces per environment (dev/staging/prod) with state locking to an S3-compatible backend. For on-prem customers who insist on local state, we will refuse unless they adopt a supported remote-locking backend — highlight this in the contract.

- VLANs/CIDR: suggest a hard rule: no cross-environment overlapping CIDRs. If Acme insists on overlapping ranges for isolated racks, we will need explicit NAT/proxy prescriptive steps — call this out as an exception that needs network-owner signoff.

I will add inline comments to the contract PDF and push a proposed policy linter MR.

Irene
Principal PM, Private Deploy
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Kyle Turner <kyle@acme-edge.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — contract items + CI gating for VLAN segregation

Quick operational catch from Networking:

- GitLab runners: the air-gap mirror job must run on a runner that uses the on-prem NAT exclusion list; we'll provide a runner config snippet. It also needs a short-lived token to push images into the mirror — don't bake tokens into the pipeline. We'll require a vault-based retrieval step.
- Helm values: require an automated validation job that checks helmValues.yaml for any exposed hostnames or external load balancer settings. If a chart contains an external LB, pipeline should fail and require explainer in MR description.
- Rollbacks: include a mandatory "module-rollback-check" stage that runs a smoke test against a scratch VLAN to confirm no control-plane changes leak across boundaries.

Putting these into a small MR for the infra repo; ETA EOD tomorrow. If procurement needs the updated contract today, we can ship a redlined summary that lists these as binding conditions.

—Marcus
Staff Network Engineer, Redwood Inf.
From: Kyle Turner <kyle@acme-edge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.procure@acme-edge.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, devops@acme-edge.com

Subject: Re: Private deploy — contract items + CI gating for VLAN segregation

Folks — this is great, thanks for the quick turnaround. Two asks before we close procurement: 

1) Can you provide the MR link that implements the policy linter and the runner config snippet (we want to include that in our security pack)?
2) For the exception path (overlapping CIDRs in isolated racks), please add the precise text we should expect in the contract to avoid ambiguity.

I'll queue procurement hold until we get the MR and the redline language. If you can push both by EOD tomorrow we'll target signing Friday.

Thanks all — Kyle
